title: Optimize PrimitiveMesh creation by avoiding CoW behavior and dynamic memory allocations
body:
I was profiling culling performance which required me to generated 20,000 Meshes at startup. I noticed that startup was taking a very long time (even with an optimized build). So I profiled it and found that half the time for generating Primitive meshes is spent in `Vector::push_back`. This is both because of the CoW behaviour and the memory allocations. Simply using LocalVectors and then converting to Vectors before returning the data roughly doubles performance. 

More can be done to optimize these functions, but anything else would require a lot more intrusive changes and wouldn't yield the same benefit. 

Running a quick benchmark (time to generate 2000 instances) over the changed Mesh types I get:

Before (4.4.1):
```
SphereMesh
1.05062
BoxMesh
0.046538
CapsuleMesh
0.902834
CylinderMesh
0.246506
PlaneMesh
0.036552
PrismMesh
0.040652
TorusMesh
0.988274
TubeTrailMesh
0.163032
RibbonTrailMesh
0.097105
```
After (non-dev build but no LTO):
```
SphereMesh
0.535162
BoxMesh
0.042593
CapsuleMesh
0.469328
CylinderMesh
0.146048
PlaneMesh
0.03898
PrismMesh
0.040443
TorusMesh
0.54022
TubeTrailMesh
0.096121
RibbonTrailMesh
0.074852
```
_note: Box, Plane, and Prism don't really change because they all were tested with default settings, With a higher subdivision, the difference is noticeable._


<details>
  <summary>test script</summary>

```
func _ready() -> void:
	print("SphereMesh")
	var time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = SphereMesh.new()
		mesh.radius = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)
	
	print("BoxMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = BoxMesh.new()
		mesh.size.x = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)
	
	print("CapsuleMesh")

		mesh.radius = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)

	print("CylinderMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = CylinderMesh.new()
		mesh.height = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)
	
	print("PlaneMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = PlaneMesh.new()
		mesh.size.x = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)

	print("PrismMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = PrismMesh.new()
		mesh.size.x = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)

	print("TorusMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = TorusMesh.new()
		mesh.inner_radius = 0.2
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)

	print("TubeTrailMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = TubeTrailMesh.new()
		mesh.radius = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)

	print("RibbonTrailMesh")
	time = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	for i in range(num_instances):
		var mesh = RibbonTrailMesh.new()
		mesh.size = 0.5
		var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
		mesh_instance.mesh = mesh
	print((Time.get_ticks_usec()-time)/1000000.0)

```
</details>
